36129e53-d7d5-4f1e-b749-ce9994f5c096.headline: Sparrow killed Revenant and Dekker eight times, no ally died after the early duo trades, and Fangtooth and Mini Prime went to the team.

flags.text: Sparrow was a damn menace: nine kills, one death, the game's most gold, plus the duo outer tower.
Crunch dealt the most hero damage in the game, 13135, and mitigated the most, 12875, on one death.
Feng Mao dealt 15483 of the team's 17873 objective damage; the enemy team dealt zero.
The team cleared zero of the enemy's 20 wards all game, while Drongo cleared an allied ward.

focus.title: A tower after every clean fight
focus.action: After a fight won with no deaths, hit the nearest outer tower before resetting, and sweep enemy wards off the duo lane before early fights there, where three of four allied deaths came.

12.1.call: Sparrow killed Dekker, then Revenant, with no allied deaths, won 2-0. The team took Fangtooth after the fight.

13.3.call: Lt. Belica killed Revenant and Sparrow killed Dekker, won 2-0 with no allied deaths, after Fangtooth had already gone to the team. No tower, Fangtooth or Prime followed inside ninety seconds.

14.5.call: Two separate plays: Crunch killed Greystone on the offlane, and Sparrow killed Revenant and Drongo on the duo lane. Mini Prime went to the team, and Sparrow is credited with the duo outer tower within the minute.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Hero damage ran 708 per minute against a norm of 920. After a takedown resets basic cooldowns through Endless Hunt, fire Piercing Shot or Hail of Arrows next.
Only death: Drongo, on the duo lane, in the opening fight lost 1-2. When Drongo is missing from the map early, ward the duo-side river before fighting Dekker there.
bfbe9162-5721-48af-a087-0e123c33735b: Hell of a turnaround: first blood went to Greystone, then two kills on Greystone on the offlane and no second death.
Once the enemy offlane outer fell, the mid kill on Iggy & Scorch put the open lane to use. Repeat that rotation whenever the offlane tower goes first.
f67438f5-0f92-4204-bd3b-f90138549796: Most healing in the game at 9873 and the most assists at eight, with a hand in 56 percent of the team's kills.
Two deaths on the duo lane before minute ten, to Drongo and to Revenant; duo deaths before ten finished even at three apiece.
Ten wards, the most in the game, still sit under the norm of 16. Sanctification allows three at once; keep the third covering the duo lane.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Zero deaths, two kills and 10.3 CS per minute against a norm of 7.9, in a mid lane rated unfavored on paper.
Hero damage ran 348 per minute against a norm of 728, under half. Next game, spend Void Bomb and Seismic Assault on Iggy & Scorch whenever the lane is safe.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Zero deaths, credited with the enemy offlane outer tower, then a Drongo kill within the half minute after the tower fell.
Hero damage ran 175 per minute against a norm of 556. Sparrow scored nine of the team's 16 kills; after an objective, join Sparrow's next fight for damage.

matchup: Duo was Sparrow and Mourn against Revenant and Dekker; Revenant and Dekker never killed Sparrow.
Revenant's Scar roots once all Marked stacks are consumed, and Reckoning banishes a hero into the Nether Realm.
build: Lightning Hawk and Tainted Rounds sit off the winning core of Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra.
Tainted Rounds cuts the target's healing 45% on basic attacks; Greystone and Drongo were the enemy's top healers.
No completed item or the crest carries armor or health.
eternal: Weald's true-damage missiles fire on damaging a hero below 30% health.
Wind-Rider adds attack speed on leaving the Stealth from Heightened Senses; Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill.
Weald sits in a field toss-up led by Thraex, and Forage with Wind-Rider is Weald's best pair. Sound keep.
augment: Endless Hunt resets basic ability cooldowns on takedowns and adds permanent physical penetration; nine kills and two assists here.
Sun Shards is the field's Best on Sparrow carry: ricocheting basic attacks, giving up the resets and penetration.
crest: Liberator cleanses all debuffs and grants a shield, an answer to the root from Revenant's Scar.
Pacifier leans ahead in the field, with Eviscerator next and Liberator behind: a dash and empowered hit instead of the cleanse.
improvement: Sound keep on Weald and the items; a one-death game proves no build change.
Sun Shards for Endless Hunt is the field-backed swap, trading takedown resets for ricochet damage.
Pacifier for Liberator adds a dash and low-health burst, giving up the cleanse against Scar's root.

matchup: Greystone was the lane opponent and finished 1/2/0 with 12567 hero damage, both deaths to Crunch.
Greystone's Make Way shreds physical armor in stacks, and Stoicism deflects a basic attack on a cooldown.
Greystone built Overlord and Augmentation, two max-health items.
build: Augmentation and Mutilator are two of the three winning-core items; Salvation is the missing third.
Mutilator deals 1% max health per basic attack and applies three times on ability hits, a match for Greystone's health items.
Augmentation empowers the next basic attack after an ability cast, the same rhythm as Cross Crunch.
eternal: Weald adds a true-damage volley against heroes under 30% health, with an extra missile per 30% bonus attack speed.
Wind-Rider triggers after a dash such as Forward Crunch; Forage pays out on minion and monster kills.
Weald trails the Crunch offlane field, a toss-up led by Pilow with Knell, Nihil and Demiurge close behind.
augment: Combo Crunch stacks attack speed off Cross Crunch damage, and holds the best odds in a toss-up with Lunge Crunch. Sound keep.
crest: Judgement hits an area around Crunch and heals per hero struck, with later hits at half effect.
Gravitum leads a field toss-up with Iceskorn Talons; Judgement, the most played, trails the pair.
improvement: Took 19794 damage, the most in the game, with no armor item; test an armor item third against Greystone, Revenant and Drongo.
Salvation, the missing core item, adds health, tenacity and a low-health shield, but no armor.
Pilow for Weald is the field-backed Eternal swap: ability casts weaken nearby enemy damage, giving up the execute missiles.

matchup: Duo was Mourn and Sparrow against Dekker and Revenant; Mourn killed Revenant once and died to Drongo and to Revenant.
Dekker's Stasis Bomb stuns, Containment Fence blocks enemy heroes from passing, and Ion Strike stuns in the center.
Dekker placed seven wards against Mourn's ten, and the two supports cleared zero wards apiece.
build: Elafrost is the single completed item, off the winning core of Megacosm, Astral Catalyst and Tainted Scepter.
Elafrost adds 45 physical armor against three physical damage dealers; Frostblade empowers a basic attack after ability casts and slows.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health growing with level; Festering Wounds makes damage over time and immobilizing effects cut enemy healing 45%.
Contagion deals damage over time, so Festering Wounds has a trigger; Cannibalism adds 25 maximum health per takedown.
The engine does not model support Eternals; Lotus leans ahead of Knell in the Mourn support field, with Krix behind.
augment: Nightstalker raises the bonus movement speed of Eclipse.
Nightmare Extractor leans ahead in the field: ability casts shorten Extract's cooldown, giving up the Eclipse speed.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields nearby heroes and adds tenacity while the shield holds; Visionary raises the ward cap from two to three.
Tranquility is the field's Best Mourn support crest: a group heal plus damage mitigation, with the same ward cap.
improvement: Tranquility for Sanctification is the field-backed swap, trading the group shield and tenacity for a group heal.
Lotus for Krix leads the field, giving up the Festering Wounds anti-heal.

matchup: Iggy & Scorch was the mid opponent: Lt. Belica killed Iggy & Scorch once, and Iggy & Scorch finished with zero kills.
Oil Spill slows, Inferno ends in a Belch that knocks heroes back, and Flame Turrets shoot fireballs.
build: Combustion is one of three winning-core items; Noxia and Wraith Leggings were not completed.
Combustion's Pyro hits the target and nearby enemies on ability damage, and damaging heroes shortens Pyro's cooldown.
eternal: Aion stacks mana regeneration on spell casts and turns 6% of spell damage on enemy heroes into gold.
Bottomless Vial gives a potion charge and magical power per River Buff kill; Runic Focus scales magical power with current mana.
Lotus leads a Lt. Belica mid toss-up with Xyris; Aion trails, though Bottomless Vial with Runic Focus is Aion's best pair.
augment: Combat Veteran grants passive experience every second, rising with hero level.
Combat Veteran is clearly the field's best Lt. Belica mid augment. Sound keep.
crest: The recorded crest was Wizard Crest, still unevolved: enough mana restored from ability hits and kills, then a base visit, evolves.
Epoch evolves from Wizard Crest; Typhoon leans ahead of Epoch in the field but evolves from Warlock Crest.
improvement: Evolve the crest at the first base visit once ready; Wizard Crest trails every evolved mid crest with enough field games.
No item swap is proven here; the crest evolution is the clear fix.

matchup: Drongo was the jungle opponent: two kills, all in the opening duo fight, and two deaths, to Sparrow and to Feng Mao.
Drongo's Gag Grenade silences, and Shrapnel Cannon shreds physical armor and pushes enemies back.
Greystone, Revenant and Drongo deal physical damage, and no completed item carries armor.
build: Manta Scythe is one of three winning-core items; Omen and The Perforator were not completed.
Manta Scythe's Divide & Conquer adds 8% damage against isolated enemy units; Insatiable Harvest speeds minion and small-monster clears.
eternal: Demiurge raises item stats and item-effect damage by 10%; Construct adds health and ability haste per level.
Bloatware adds damage and damage reduction per item, so a single completed item keeps the bonus small.
Demiurge leans ahead in the Feng Mao jungle field, and Construct with Bloatware is Demiurge's best pair. Sound keep.
augment: Imperial Duelist debuffs basic-attack targets; against debuffed targets, Feng Mao deals 5% more damage and takes 5% less.
Imperial Duelist holds the best odds in a field toss-up with Ichorous Glaive. Sound keep.
crest: Ortus's Limit Breaker grants movement speed and physical power for a short window, with permanent power per takedown inside the window.
Ortus is the field's Best Feng Mao jungle crest, ahead of Nex. Sound keep.
improvement: Augment, Eternal and crest sit at or near the top of the Feng Mao jungle field. Sound keep.
Against three physical damage dealers, an armor item before Omen is the swap to test, giving up Omen's cooldown cuts.

5e1df3fa-f82c-4eb8-a58e-47b3e9166b12.headline: Two inhibitors down, no fucking finish, then five bodies traded for Orb Prime while they walked mid to our Core.

focus.title: Close with five, play through Belica
focus.action: Once an inhibitor falls, walk five to the next structure and the Core before Orb Prime, never start a fight a player down, play through Lt. Belica and keep Kira covered against Serath.

15.5.call: Legion killed Renna and Lt. Belica killed Serath; Sparrow killed Legion and Steel killed Muriel. The fight went 3-1 and the team took the Fangtooth less than a minute later. Legion and Steel both scored away from home lanes before either lane had opened.

34.4.call: Sparrow killed Steel and Serath killed Kira with no enemy deaths. Within the next minute the team took the enemy duo-lane inner tower and inhibitor, and the enemy took the second Primal Fangtooth.

36.6.call: Renna killed Legion and Lt. Belica, Sparrow killed Aurora at the Prime pit and Serath killed Steel, with no enemy deaths, while the team took the Orb Prime. Shortly after, the enemy took two inner towers, an inhibitor and the Core.

matchup: Terra was the lane opponent, killed Legion three times and mitigated the most damage in the game.
Wild Rush is Unstoppable while channeling; Unstoppable Force cleanses debuffs, disables nearby towers and adds both armors and tenacity.
Terra's Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone basic-attacking Terra, which taxes a rifle hero.
build: Every item carries physical penetration, raising rifle damage and clearing the Orbital Sanction radius threshold; the physical power clears Saturation Charge's too.
Deathstalker's shred, Viper's Corrode and The Perforator's armor ignore all cut into Terra's armor.
Mesmer adds health and a spell shield that blocks the next ability.
eternal: Thraex suits a rifle that keeps firing on one target: more damage to the marked hero, less damage back.
Golden Mane is the draft alternative to Rallying Roar: less single-target damage taken, giving up the group speed burst.
augment: Scorched Earth's napalm pays when enemies hold ground, such as around an objective, and adds little against a retreating target.
Press the Advantage is the alternative: takedown Rally Points boost fire rate and ally attack speed, giving up napalm and the heal.
crest: Ortus grants a burst of movement speed and physical power; a takedown inside the window refreshes the burst and adds permanent power.
Ortus offers no defense, so against Terra's engage the speed only helps chase or reposition.
improvement: No completed item has armor, while Terra, Serath and Sparrow deal mostly physical damage.
If Terra or Serath keep winning exchanges, compare Draconum for Viper: armor and takedown healing, losing attack speed, penetration, Corrode and Diligence.
Mesmer is a sound keep, since the spell shield can block Renna's Stupor or Terra's Highland Hurl.

matchup: Duo was Steel and Kira against Sparrow and Muriel; Steel killed Sparrow three times, the most by any ally.
Muriel's charged Serenity stuns, and Reversal Of Fortune shields any ally from anywhere and knocks up on arrival.
Renna killed Steel three times, more than either duo opponent, and Serath killed Kira five times.
build: Tainted Charm cuts healing on enemy heroes near Steel, covering Muriel's heals and Serath, the game's top healer.
Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone basic-attacking Steel, such as Serath or Sparrow.
Vainglory is the only magical armor item against Renna's magical damage; three armor items feed Heavy Metal.
eternal: Krix scales the health that Raiment of Renewal, Tainted Charm and Fire Blossom stack.
Cannibalism paid steadily with fourteen takedowns.
Festering Wounds adds little here, since Steel already carried two anti-heal items.
augment: Heavy Metal turns Steel's total armor into bonus magical damage on heavy punches and Shield Bash.
Adaptive Force is the alternative against three ranged enemies: two smaller Force Shield charges, giving up the armor-based damage.
crest: Rift Walkers dashes and pulls nearby heroes toward Steel, setting up Shield Bash or Shield Slam.
Against Serath on Kira, the pull can drag a diver off the carry.
The crest adds Solstone and raises the ward cap from two to three for the game's top ward placer.
improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves, and Steel built none of the three.
Xenia for Raiment of Renewal shields allies beside Steel and adds both armors, giving up health, regeneration, tenacity and some haste.

matchup: Serath, the jungle opponent, tied for the most kills in the game and had the most healing.
Serath vanishes during Heaven's Fury and teleports to the marked target, so Aurora's roots and Cryoseism stun land once Serath reappears.
Wild Rush channels Unstoppable, so control into it is wasted; Unstoppable Force cleanses on cast, then adds tenacity.
build: Spectral Schematics and Dynamo both trigger on immobilizing, which Hoarfrost, Glacial Thorns and Cryoseism supply.
Flux Matrix halves nearby enemy tenacity and adds magical damage taken, cutting the tenacity Terra's Unstoppable Force grants.
Dynamo, Elafrost and Flux Matrix cover both physical and magical armor.
eternal: Flawless and Fragrance suit a jungler fighting inside spell range; eleven takedowns fed Lotus.
Immaculate is the draft alternative to Fragrance: damage reduction near full health, giving up close-range damage.
augment: Hypothermia is the alternative: Boreal Sweep cuts armor and the attack speed Sparrow and Serath lean on, giving up that root.
crest: Tempest pays when Aurora stays in contact for the full duration, healing off the damage.
Muriel's damaging abilities and Sparrow's Tainted Rounds can cut that healing.
improvement: Nothing argues for a swap: two deaths and the winning core in place.
If a later lobby has no tenacity or magical-damage target to answer, reconsider Flux Matrix; here the item is a sound keep.

matchup: Renna took first blood on Lt. Belica and killed Lt. Belica once more; Lt. Belica killed Renna three times.
Renna spends mana on every active ability, so Void Drone's mana drain and Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage have a target.
Renna finished second in hero damage, behind Lt. Belica.
build: Seismic Assault, Void Bomb and Neural Disruptor supply the separate ability hit Noxia's bonus needs.
Caustica ignores a share of magical armor from Terra's Transference and Inquisition and Muriel's Devotion.
Megacosm's bonus-health burn answers Terra's health stacking; otherwise this is a pure output build.
eternal: Aion turns spell damage on heroes into gold, and Lt. Belica led the game in hero damage and finished second in gold.
Philosopher is the draft alternative to Bottomless Vial: steady passive gold without needing river buffs.
augment: Combat Veteran is pure scaling: a little movement speed and passive experience, with no fight effect.
Devastating Bombs is the fight-side alternative: harder Void Bomb hits on isolated targets, giving up the experience and speed.
crest: Soulbearer's shield, magical lifesteal and speed are self-sustain for a hero with no dash beyond Blink.
Sparrow's Tainted Rounds can cut the lifesteal half, so the shield buys the time against Sparrow and Serath.
improvement: Hold the core: hero damage per minute more than double the recorded Lt. Belica norm.
If Serath or Sparrow end fights early, compare Golem's Gift for Megacosm: physical armor and more power, giving up health and burns.
If Renna is the problem, magical armor is the comparison instead.

matchup: Kira killed Sparrow twice and Muriel once, and Sparrow killed Kira once.
Serath was the real threat, killing Kira five times, more than any other enemy.
During Purge, Kira can cast no ability except Shadow Glide and is slowed, so a channel with Serath unseen limits the exits.
build: An all-crit basic-attack build with no armor or health on any item.
Terminus turns excess lifesteal healing into a shield, the only defense in the build.
Terra's Tainted Guard cuts healing on anyone basic-attacking Terra, starving that lifesteal.
eternal: Melting Point only pays above a high armor threshold, which Terra's three armor items alone pass.
Sub-Surface is the draft alternative: less damage from area abilities like Hail Of Arrows and Heresy, giving up the bonus against Terra.
augment: Bringer Of Mercy cuts current cooldowns when Mercy deals damage, bringing Shadow Glide back sooner.
Siphoning Purge is the sustain alternative, giving up the cooldown cuts; Muriel's damaging abilities would reduce that healing.
crest: Pacifier is a second dash beside Shadow Glide and Blink, the escape the build otherwise lacks against Serath.
improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator; Kira had Imperator.
Ashbringer for Dust Devil cuts cooldowns on basic attacks, returning Shadow Glide faster, giving up movement speed, some attack speed and Menace.

2a22df0b-99f2-43ae-a75e-d8826267a85e: Finished the enemy offlane outer tower and offlane inhibitor, the first enemy inhibitor we took, and picked up 4 kills away from the offlane.
7 deaths, over the norm, 3 to Terra, in a lane the sim read as theirs all game. First down in the Orb Prime collapse, to Renna in their half.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Ran the vision: 26 wards placed and 5 cleared, both game highs, plus a hand in over half our kills and no early-game deaths.
5 deaths, over the norm, 3 to Renna. One came outside any detected fight, and the next fight started a player down and went 2-3.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Most objective damage in the game, farmed well over the norm and died only twice, the fewest on the team.
Both deaths came in objective windows: to Serath shortly before their second Fangtooth, and to Sparrow at the Prime pit as we took Orb Prime.
4 wards placed, under the norm. If wards were equipped, spend them on the pit approaches before every Fangtooth and Prime.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: The team's damage: most hero damage in the game, over double the norm, tied with Serath for the most kills. Fucking filthy.
Once mid opened, took 3 kills on the duo lane; the team took their mid inner, duo outer and offlane inhibitor soon after. Keep looking for that play.
c41ac3b0-b320-4995-885d-3958557014f8: Died 10 times against a norm of 7 and posted the team's lowest kill participation at 32%.
Farm ran well over the norm at 7.6 CS per minute against 5.6. Two deaths to Serath came right before their first Fangtooth and only Primal Fangtooth.

flags.text: Offlane and duo inhibitors down, their mid inner gone too, and we never once hit their Core.
Orb Prime over the Core: five of us died in that minute, then they walked mid.
Two of the last four fights started a player down; the one deep in their half lost 2-3.
Kira had a carry game to forget: ten deaths, five to Serath, the least gold of either carry.

68e713af-33d7-4758-a70c-930b5533b994.headline: The duo lane got fucking farmed: Kira and Steel took nine of the eleven team deaths, and not one fight was won.

flags.text: Zinx and Eden scored eight of the enemy's eleven kills, every one on Kira or Steel.
The enemy took the opening kill in four of five fights, every time on Steel.
The team took six of the first eight river buffs; the enemy took all six after that.
Bayle's rotation kill on Zinx answered Kira's death in the duo lane, and Bayle never died.

focus.title: Fix the duo before contesting river
focus.action: When the duo keeps dying, send the jungler or the offlaner there before contesting the next river buff, and have Kira and Steel give up the wave until help arrives.

3.call: Zinx killed Steel, Kira killed Zinx and Eden killed Kira on the duo side; Grux killed The Fey in mid. Two separate plays, both lost, and the team took a river buff in the same window.

6.5.call: Zinx killed Steel and Eden killed Kira on the duo side, with no enemy deaths. The team took a river buff in the same window.

8.3.call: Kira killed Eden, Zinx killed Kira and Grux killed The Fey within seconds, a fight lost one kill to two, while the team took the only Fangtooth of the game.

11.8.call: Gideon killed Steel, Eden killed Kira, Kira killed Grux and Bayle killed Zinx on the duo side, an even trade at two kills each. The enemy took a river buff in the same window.

14.8.call: Zinx killed Steel and Kira with no enemy deaths, the last kills of the game, and the enemy took two river buffs in the same window.

5c8cbd99-c52b-428d-87cc-fcfca4d654a1: Hero damage ran 324 per minute against a norm of 817, while Gideon, the mid opponent, dealt the most hero damage in the game.
Both deaths came to Grux, fewer than the norm. Next game, chain Harvest Nettles on the same hero: each repeat hit within eight seconds stacks more damage.
945f7a88-d3eb-40fc-a02a-2449feddf549: Zero deaths against a norm above four, the only laner who never died.
Hero damage ran 361 per minute against a norm of 606; Serath, the lane opponent, finished without a kill or death. When the offlane is quiet, repeat the duo rotation.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Zero deaths and 6290 objective damage, the most in the game, while the team took the game's only Fangtooth.
Hero damage ran 155 per minute against a norm of 521, with two assists in five team kills.
Two wards placed against a norm of 6.9, but two enemy wards cleared, the most in the game. If wards were equipped, cover the duo-side river.
9df9186c-d73f-4f00-a546-daa15a642f41: Five deaths, the most in the game: three to Eden, two to Zinx. Favored on paper against Eden, but Eden won the kills three to one.
Still the team's sharpest weapon: three of the five team kills, one each on Zinx, Eden and Grux, and the most hero damage on the team.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: A hand in two of the five team kills and the most damage mitigated on the team, but four deaths, three to Zinx, including first blood.
Three wards placed against a norm of six, and none cleared. If a sentry was equipped, sweep the duo-side river before trading with Zinx and Eden.

matchup: Eden out-damaged Kira, 9659 hero damage to 8191, with six assists to none for Kira.
Eden's melee stance heals off hero damage, and Eden's Vanquisher executes heroes left at very low health.
Zinx's Neural Regenesis revives an ally on lethal damage, so a kill on Eden can be undone.
build: Nothing in the build, crest included, carries armor or health, against Eden's physical damage.
Ashbringer's basic attacks cut non-ultimate cooldowns, more on critical strikes, so Shadow Glide returns sooner.
Lightning Hawk builds charge while moving or attacking, and the charged basic attack adds damage and a slow.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Kira damages a hero below a health threshold, a finisher on low targets.
Wind-Rider adds attack speed after a dash, which Shadow Glide supplies; Dryad's Boon trims basic ability cooldowns on hit.
Natural Resistance is the first-minor alternative into Zinx's Ricochet stun: a cleanse at low health, giving up Dryad's Boon.
augment: Lenore makes Shadow Glide refresh Nevermore, the Raven shot that hits for a share of the target's current health.
Bringer Of Mercy is the field's most-run Kira augment: Mercy hits cut current cooldowns, giving up the Raven refresh.
crest: Assassin Crest is the base tier: health back on ability hits and unit kills, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Pacifier, the field's usual Kira crest, adds a dash beside Shadow Glide, plus lifesteal.
improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator; Ashbringer is in, and Lightning Hawk sits outside the core.
Solaris next adds an empowered basic attack after each ability cast that heals off the damage dealt.
If Eden keeps winning trades, compare Draconum: physical armor and takedown healing, giving up the critical chance Solaris or Imperator adds.

matchup: Duo was Steel and Kira against Zinx and Eden; before minute ten, the duo died five times to the enemy duo's two.
Zinx's Ricochet stuns the first enemy hit and bounces to more targets, and Bad Medicine slows twice in a pool.
Gideon took the other Steel death; Gideon's Black Hole pulls nearby enemies in while channeling.
build: Xenia shields an ally hero standing close by and adds both armors, health and ability haste.
Xenia's armor also feeds Heavy Metal's bonus damage and Cybernetic Shell's hybrid armor scaling.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health that grows with level; Regenerative Tissue regenerates after a stretch without hero damage.
Cannibalism paid twice: two takedowns, two permanent health stacks.
Festering Wounds is the first-minor alternative: Steel's stuns would cut healing on Eden, giving up the regeneration.
augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage to heavy punches and Shield Bash, scaling with Steel's total armor; the field's most-run pick.
Bulldozer is the alternative: damage reduction during Bull Rush, giving up the armor-scaled damage.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields Steel and nearby heroes and grants tenacity while the shield holds, against Zinx's stuns.
Sanctification raises the ward cap, a bonus that pays only when wards keep going down; three went down all game.
improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves; Xenia was the one finished.
Dynamo next makes each immobilized enemy take more damage, a payoff for the Shield Bash and Shield Slam stuns.

matchup: Grux was the jungle opponent: two kills, both on The Fey, one death to Kira, and the most damage taken.
Grux's Double Pain heals per hero hit, and Grux had the most healing in the game.
Eden, Serath and Grux deal physical damage, and neither Spirit Of Amir nor Warlock Crest carries armor.
build: Spirit Of Amir gives magical lifesteal inside the jungle, magical power outside the jungle, and more ability damage to monsters.
The monster damage suits the most objective damage in the game; against Eden's physical damage the item adds health but no armor.
eternal: Lotus grants a small random bonus on a timer and on each takedown; two takedowns fed Lotus.
Flawless heals Aurora and nearby allies on ability hits against heroes; Fragrance adds magical damage to nearby heroes.
Krix with Predator is the field's most-run Aurora jungle Eternal: more health, giving up Flawless's group healing.
augment: Glacial Thorns makes Glacial Charge spawn crystals that damage and briefly root, the field's most-run pick.
Hypothermia is the alternative into Grux: Boreal Sweep shreds both armors and slows attack speed, giving up that root.
crest: Warlock Crest is the base tier: health back on ability damage and unit kills, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Tempest is the field's most-run Aurora jungle crest: a burn on nearby heroes that heals off the damage.
improvement: The winning core is Spirit Of Amir, Magnify and Spectral Schematics; Spirit Of Amir was the one finished.
If Eden or Grux keep landing hits, compare Golem's Gift next: physical armor and magical power, giving up Magnify's health and omnivamp.

matchup: Serath was the lane opponent; Bayle out-damaged Serath, 5420 hero damage to 3902.
Serath's Heaven's Fury grants invulnerability and control immunity while vanished, so hold Cursed Edge's stun until Serath reappears.
Skull Crusher shreds the armor of marked enemies, useful against Grux, the game's sturdiest frontline.
build: Manta Scythe adds physical power, penetration, attack speed and lifesteal, plus bonus damage to minions and small monsters.
Divide & Conquer adds damage against a target with no nearby ally, so isolated targets pay.
Goliath Crest's small armor is the only armor in the build, against three physical damage dealers.
eternal: Nihil's Doom stacks power and both armors while Bayle keeps damaging heroes; takedowns and level-ups raise the gains permanently.
From the Abyss regenerates health in hero combat or out of enemy vision; Adaptive Plating adds armor matching damage taken.
Thraex with Alpha's Court and Ferocity is the field's most-run Bayle offlane setup, trading Nihil's armor for solo damage and attack speed.
augment: Frenzied Fighter keeps Berserk on with no cooldown while under the health threshold, the field's most-run pick.
Betrayer's Reqiuem is the alternative for grouped fights: Kingslayer uppercuts everyone around the target, giving up endless Berserk.
crest: Goliath Crest is the base tier: health back on taking damage or killing units, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Judgement is the field's most-run Bayle offlane crest: an area hit that heals per hero struck.
improvement: The winning core is Tainted Blade, Rapture and Cursed Scroll; Bayle finished none of the three.
Tainted Blade next cuts healing on every physical hit, against Grux's Double Pain and Zinx's Infuse on Eden.
Cursed Scroll adds both armors and health regeneration, the core's answer to three physical damage dealers.

matchup: Gideon was the mid opponent: 9963 hero damage to The Fey's 4867, and The Fey killed Gideon once.
Gideon's Black Hole pulls nearby enemies while channeling, and Torn Space opens a portal allies can follow through.
Grux killed The Fey twice; Smash 'n Grab pulls and stuns, and Stampede drags heroes along the dash.
build: Combustion adds magical power, penetration and mana, and Pyro bursts the target and nearby enemies on ability damage.
Pyromaniac shortens Pyro's cooldown on hero damage, so Combustion pays most when abilities keep landing on heroes.
eternal: Aion turns spell damage on heroes into gold, so hero damage under half the norm meant less Aion gold.
Philosopher drips passive gold; Arcane Resonance speeds basic ability cooldowns and Philosopher with mana regeneration.
Bottomless Vial is the field's most-run Aion first minor: river buffs refill a potion and add magical power, giving up Philosopher.
augment: Wild Growth extends Bramble Patch's range, the field's most-run pick for the slow zone.
Natural Infusion is the alternative for long trades with Gideon: Harvest Nettles hits on heroes stack ability haste, giving up range.
crest: Epoch's Stasis Device puts The Fey in stasis briefly; Epoch is the field's most-run The Fey mid crest.
Soulbearer is the alternative: a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed, giving up the stasis.
improvement: The winning core is Combustion, Wraith Leggings and Megacosm; Combustion was the one finished.
Wraith Leggings next adds magical power, penetration and bonus ability damage on low-health heroes, the core path to closing the damage gap.
Two deaths, fewer than the norm, so no defensive swap is called for; the build path is a sound keep.

a6b217f3-0fbe-40e9-8724-d93021debb0f.headline: Feng Mao fed on the solo laners all game, 15 kills and 46137 objective damage, while the whole team managed 9560 objective damage.

flags.text: Shinbi died eight times, seven to Feng Mao, six on the offlane. Same damn jungler.
Offlane and duo side collapsed in one window: five deaths, zero kills, then two inner towers and Fangtooth.
Wraith died eight times, five to Feng Mao, and trailed Lt. Belica in gold, 13.7k to 15.6k.
A seven-kill lead after Mini Prime never became gold: team gold finished 71.2k against 84.8k.

focus.title: Track Feng Mao, spend leads on towers
focus.action: When Feng Mao is missing from the map, offlane and mid play back toward the tower behind river wards; when the team leads on kills, group five for the enemy mid outer tower, never taken.

12.6.call: Serath killed Lt. Belica and Feng Mao, Wraith killed Gadget, and Feng Mao killed Shinbi, won 3-1, with Mini Prime to the team in the same window. The one won fight, and the one prize cashed.

25.4.call: Five allied deaths and zero kills across the offlane and the duo lane, two separate plays. Two lanes losing bodies at once is the signal to give up both waves and hold the inner towers together.

30.1.call: Feng Mao killed Shinbi and TwinBlast killed Wraith, lost 0-2, and Orb Prime went to the enemy in the same window. Near a Prime the enemy can take, the solo laners group before fighting.

31.9.call: Feng Mao killed Serath in the team's jungle and TwinBlast killed Wraith on the mid lane, lost 0-2, and the mid inner tower and mid inhibitor fell within the minute. Two down that late, the other three defend under the next structure instead of opening a fight 3v5.

8f8a1346-8011-411c-aa95-f6d7de6b4c86: Hell of a lane against Aurora: four kills, zero deaths to Aurora, the enemy offlane outer tower, and the team's most gold and hero damage.
Deaths ran more than double the hero norm. One kill on Aurora was followed within the half minute by a death to Feng Mao on the offlane.
After any offlane kill with Feng Mao missing from the map, ward the offlane-side river entrance and back off to the tower before taking the next wave.
58cd21d0-6b1f-449b-a598-94cc33d52ec6: Opened strong: four kills on Lt. Belica, a kill on Feng Mao, and Mini Prime in the window of the team's only won fight.
Four enemy wards cleared, the team's most, against one placed. One death to Feng Mao came outside a detected fight, in the same minute the team's mid outer tower fell.
Genesis Core and the last Fangtooth fell with no ally dead. On the next uncontested enemy major, call a contest or a counter-take on the far side of the map.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Ran the vision: 27 wards, the most in the game, and three kills on Lt. Belica without a single death to Lt. Belica.
Six mid lane deaths: three to Feng Mao, three to TwinBlast. The rotation to the offlane, enemy mid outer standing, lost no mid structure but ended in a death.
With a Sonar Drone down, hold the mid wave inside drone range; when Feng Mao or TwinBlast leaves vision, step back toward the tower before the next Knock, Knock! shot.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: The farm was there: 9.5 CS per minute against a norm of 6.8, and two deaths against a norm near four.
Zero objective damage all game while TwinBlast posted 12796, and hero damage ran 595 per minute against a norm of 900.
A rotation kill on TwinBlast in mid came 9 seconds after a Wraith death there. When the duo wave is pushed and Gadget shows elsewhere, hit the duo tower.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Most damage mitigated in the game at 45865, plus 6899 healing and zero deaths before minute ten.
Seven wards to Gadget's 21 and zero cleared, with a hand in 22 percent of the team's kills.
Before each Fangtooth, place the third ward Sanctification allows on the pit approaches; the enemy took all three Fangtooths.

matchup: Aurora was the lane opponent: four kills for Shinbi, zero for Aurora, and Shinbi out-earned Aurora 17617 gold to 16452.
Feng Mao was the real offlane threat, with seven kills on Shinbi and the most healing in the game.
Aurora is credited with the team's offlane outer and inner towers despite zero kills on Shinbi.
build: Five completed items and zero physical armor, against Feng Mao's physical damage.
Tainted Scepter and Oathkeeper, two of the winning core, were not built.
Magnify cuts magical armor 6% per ability hit on heroes, stacking five times, and adds omnivamp.
eternal: Aion turns 6% of spell damage on enemy heroes into gold; Philosopher generates gold every 10s.
Philosopher with Arcane Resonance is Aion's best pair.
Pilow holds the best odds in a field toss-up with Aion and Vesh on Shinbi offlane.
augment: Allegro lowers Rushing Beat's cooldown by 15%, the most played Shinbi offlane augment.
Crescendo leans ahead in the field: bonus magical damage on the chain's final basic attack, giving up the faster dash.
crest: Obelisk's Condemn is an empowered basic attack; a target dying within 3s yields a Soul, and Souls add damage and magical power.
Obelisk holds the best odds in a toss-up with Soulbearer. Sound keep.
improvement: If Feng Mao keeps killing on the offlane, a physical armor item for Magnify buys survival, giving up the magical armor shred.
Tainted Scepter, from the winning core, cuts healing 45% on magical damage against Feng Mao's game-high healing.

matchup: Feng Mao was the jungle opponent: two kills on Serath, one death to Serath, and 21623 gold to 13540.
Reaping Dash hits for a share of current health, and Earth Shatter executes heroes below a health threshold.
Lt. Belica paid early: four Serath kills, all before the enemy's first tower.
build: Sky Splitter, Storm Breaker and Spectra are the full winning core, all three finished.
Draconum adds 40 physical armor against Feng Mao's physical damage, and Flow restores health on takedowns.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Serath damages a hero below 30% health.
Dryad's Boon cuts basic cooldowns on basic attack hits; Wind-Rider adds attack speed after a dash such as Heaven's Fury.
Weald is clearly the field's best Serath jungle Eternal, with Dryad's Boon and Wind-Rider the best pair. Sound keep.
augment: Crushing Descent makes Ascend stun for 0.2s on damage, and leans ahead of Vital Resonance in the field. Sound keep.
crest: Pacifier dashes and empowers the next physical hit, 2.5x against targets below 20% max health.
Liberator leans ahead of Pacifier in the field: a cleanse of all debuffs and a shield, giving up the dash.
improvement: Hero damage ran 369 per minute against a norm of 556; keep Draconum's armor while Feng Mao tops hero damage.
Liberator is the swap to test against Aurora's root and stun, giving up Pacifier's low-health burst.

matchup: Lt. Belica was the mid opponent: three kills for Wraith, zero for Lt. Belica, yet Lt. Belica out-earned Wraith 15615 to 13659.
Neural Disruptor silences and Seismic Assault stuns, the mid lane lockdown.
build: The winning core is Soulbinder, Noxia and Wraith Leggings; zero were built, and all four completed items are physical power items.
Tainted Trident cuts healing 45% on physical damage, against Feng Mao's game-high 19717 healing.
Vanquisher executes heroes taken below 5% health; Mutilator adds max-health damage on basic attacks and ability hits.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles on damaging a hero below 30% health; Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill.
Lotus leans ahead in the field on Wraith mid; Weald trails, with Forage and Wind-Rider as Weald's best pair.
augment: Sniper's Bounty adds gold on Knock, Knock! killing blows, 40 on heroes; clearly the field's best Wraith mid augment. Sound keep.
crest: Ortus grants 20% movement speed and 10% physical power for 7s; takedowns inside the window add permanent power.
Liberator holds the best odds in a toss-up with Pacifier, adding a cleanse of all debuffs; Ortus trails both.
improvement: No completed item carries armor or health; a defensive item for Mutilator is the swap to test against Feng Mao.

matchup: Duo was Drongo and Steel against TwinBlast and Gadget; zero duo deaths on either side before minute ten.
Gadget's Security Gate roots and Tesla Dome shreds magical armor; TwinBlast's Vortex Grenade slows.
Drongo's two deaths went to Gadget on the duo lane and Aurora in mid; TwinBlast never killed Drongo.
build: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Tainted Rounds are the full winning core, all three finished.
Nuclear Rounds raises ability damage 10-20% by critical chance, feeding Gag Grenade, Rad Rounds and Shrapnel Cannon.
Tainted Rounds cuts healing 45% on basic attacks, against Feng Mao's game-high healing.
eternal: Xyris adds 3% bonus damage, growing with units killed; Bone Collector adds 20% critical chance after 150 unit kills.
Xyris sits in a field toss-up with Weald and Marrow on Drongo carry; Iron Will with Bone Collector edges Furor's pair.
augment: Bring The Boom makes Rad Rounds deal 60% of the damage to nearby enemies on exploding.
Shred Spree is clearly ahead in the field: Shrapnel Cannon cooldown cut 80% for 50% less damage, giving up the splash.
crest: Pacifier dashes and empowers the next physical hit, stronger below 20% max health.
Pacifier shares a field toss-up with Liberator and Eviscerator. Sound keep.
improvement: Test Shred Spree next game: Shrapnel Cannon's physical armor shred comes far more often, at half the damage.
Full winning core finished; no item change is proven by this game, so the build stays.

matchup: Duo was Steel and Drongo against Gadget and TwinBlast; Gadget placed 21 wards to Steel's seven.
Steel killed Gadget once; Steel's three deaths went twice to TwinBlast and once to Feng Mao.
Gadget's Security Gate root and Lt. Belica's Neural Disruptor silence are the enemy's hard lockdown.
build: Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves are the full winning core, all three finished.
Xenia shields an ally hero within 200 units; Dynamo makes immobilized enemies take 8% more damage.
Flux Matrix makes nearby enemy heroes take 10% more magical damage, feeding Shinbi's magical damage.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health growing with level; Regenerative Tissue regenerates after 8s without hero damage, Cannibalism adds 25 health per takedown.
The engine does not model support Eternals; Knell and Idrisil lead the field's Steel support toss-up, with Krix the most played.
augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage to Heavy Punches and Shield Bash equal to 10% of total armor.
Colossal Crash holds the best odds in a toss-up with Heavy Metal: Shield Slam knocks back instead, giving up the armor damage.
crest: Sanctification shields Steel and nearby heroes, adds tenacity while the shield holds, and raises the ward cap to three.
Leafsong holds the best odds in a toss-up with Sanctification. Sound keep.
improvement: Sound keep on items and Krix; the augment and crest are toss-ups, so no swap is forced.

b772676f-a761-41c6-bd3c-c86847bbf4e5.headline: TwinBlast and Riktor ran Kira and Mourn over, and TwinBlast tore down the duo lane's outer tower and inhibitor.

flags.text: TwinBlast went eleven kills to one death with the most hero damage and gold in the game.
Lt. Belica killed all five enemy heroes in the final mid fight of the game.
The team took all three Fangtooths, the Orb Prime and the Genesis Core, and nine structures to one.
Only won fight with no objective or tower inside ninety seconds: TwinBlast's double kill on Kira and Mourn.

focus.title: Play through the winning lane
focus.action: Play through the lane that is winning, and after every won fight take the nearest structure if an allied minion wave is arriving, or the nearest live neutral objective if not.

20.call: TwinBlast killed Crunch and Mourn with no allied deaths. TwinBlast is credited with the enemy duo lane outer tower less than a minute later, the first structure of the game.

15.1.call: Riktor killed Kira and TwinBlast killed Mourn with no allied deaths. The team took the first Fangtooth within the minute, and TwinBlast killed Crunch, the enemy jungler, at the same moment the Fangtooth fell.

26.6.call: TwinBlast killed Crunch and Akeron and is credited with the enemy duo lane inhibitor. On the offlane, Gideon killed Greystone, Lt. Belica killed Mourn and Kira killed Lt. Belica, and Kira is credited with the allied offlane outer tower.

30.2.call: Gideon killed TwinBlast in mid, and Lt. Belica killed Gideon, Mourn, Kira, Akeron and Crunch. The team took the enemy offlane inner tower and the Core within the next minute.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Owned the duo lane: took 7 of the kills on Kira and Mourn and is the recorded destroyer of that lane's outer tower and inhibitor. Fucking ruthless.
Hero damage per minute and farm both beat the recorded norm, and the only death came in the final mid fight, to Gideon. That is the bar next game.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Most objective damage in the game at 34931, and credited with the enemy mid inhibitor.
Hero damage was the weak number: 291 per minute against a norm of 530, lowest on the team. Next game, spend Hoarfrost and Cryoseism on the target TwinBlast is hitting.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Closed the game killing all five enemy heroes in the final mid fight. A shit-hot finish, and the mid matchup with Gideon ran 3 kills to 1.
Took offlane trips once the enemy mid outer fell; the Mourn kill there answered Greystone's death. Farm ran well above the recorded norm, and mid lost no structure all game.
83cc6af5-b98c-4d37-b83c-92fc4af56366: Did the support job: a hand in over four of every five team kills, the most assists and wards placed in the game, and one death, first blood to Kira.
Cleared 1 enemy ward while Mourn placed 19. When the duo wave is shoved, sweep the duo-side river for Mourn's wards, with a sentry if one is equipped.
5b6f002b-de66-4231-9d2d-9c1f11b481c4: The wall: most damage taken, mitigated and healed in the game, one death, and farm well above the recorded norm. Akeron, the lane opponent, finished without a kill.
Kill participation is thin: one takedown in the team's 22 kills. Once the enemy offlane outer tower is down, spend the farm lead joining the next fight on another lane.

matchup: Duo was TwinBlast and Riktor against Kira and Mourn; TwinBlast killed Kira three times and Mourn four times.
Kira's Shadow Glide resets on takedowns and stacks physical power; Kira finished with two kills.
Mourn's Contagion heals and armors allies; Tainted Rounds cuts the healing of each target TwinBlast basic-attacks.
build: Solaris, Tainted Rounds and Vanquisher is the winning core, and all three were finished.
Vaporize applies on-hit effects at double effectiveness, so Sky Splitter's current-health damage lands harder through Vaporize.
Ashbringer's basic attacks shave non-ultimate cooldowns, more on critical strikes, so Gunslinger's triple shot comes up more often.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when TwinBlast damages a hero below 30% health, with extra missiles from bonus attack speed.
Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill; Wind-Rider adds attack speed after Rocket Dash.
Dryad's Boon is the first-minor alternative: basic attacks cut basic ability cooldowns, giving up the Forage farm bonus.
augment: Grenadier adds a third Vortex Grenade charge and Rocket Dash grants one, so more slows and more Gunslinger triggers.
Amplified Burst is the alternative: Vaporize gains range, giving up the extra grenade.
crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize dashes and empowers the next physical hit, far harder against targets below 20% max health.
A hero kill inside the Adrenalize window allows a recast, a fit for the top killer in the game.
improvement: Nothing to swap: the winning core finished, one death and the most hero damage in the game. Sound keep.
Sky Splitter, Imperator and Ashbringer sat outside the winning core, and nothing in this game argues against Sky Splitter, Imperator or Ashbringer.

matchup: Crunch was the jungle opponent and finished with one kill, the one on Aurora, and four deaths.
Turbo Crunch turns Right Crunch into a knockup, and Re-Crunch heals Crunch on every third hit.
The enemy ran three magical damage dealers, and Aurora carried no magical armor.
build: Spirit Of Amir, Magnify and Spectral Schematics is the winning core, and all three were finished.
Spectral Schematics and Dynamo trigger on immobilizing, which Hoarfrost's root, Cryoseism's stun and Glacial Thorns supply.
Magnify shreds magical armor on ability hits, which also helps Lt. Belica's and Riktor's magical damage.
eternal: Lotus grants a small random bonus every two minutes and on every takedown; six takedowns fed Lotus.
Flawless heals Aurora and nearby allies on ability hits against heroes, once per cast; Fragrance adds magical damage against nearby heroes.
Krix is the draft alternative: more maximum health for the jungler with the second-most damage taken in the game.
augment: Hypothermia is the alternative against Kira: Boreal Sweep shreds both armors and slows attack speed, giving up that root.
crest: Tempest's Overcharge burns up to three nearby heroes for several seconds and heals off that damage.
Overcharge pays only while enemy heroes stay inside the burn radius.
improvement: The build matches the winning core, so the build read offers no fix for the hero damage gap.
If Gideon or Akeron start focusing Aurora, compare a magical armor item for Dynamo, giving up physical armor and the immobilize amp.

matchup: Gideon was the mid opponent; Lt. Belica killed Gideon three times and died to Gideon once.
Gideon built Azure Core and Combustion, both max mana, so Void Drone's drain and Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage have a target.
Gideon scored three of the six enemy kills, the most on the enemy team, so track Gideon in fights.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings is the winning core, all finished, with Oblivion Crown raising magical power by a quarter.
Noxia's bonus needs a separate ability hit on a marked hero, which Void Bomb, Seismic Assault and Neural Disruptor supply.
Wraith Leggings adds ability damage against heroes below 40% health, suited to finishing low targets.
eternal: Vesh adds damage over time from ability damage on heroes; Mind Rot adds current-health damage on top.
Tithe of Death restores mana and stacks ability haste on takedowns; nine takedowns fed Tithe of Death.
augment: Devastating Bombs adds Void Bomb damage against isolated targets.
Combat Veteran is the alternative: movement speed and passive experience, giving up the isolated-target bomb damage.
crest: Soulbearer's Anima gives a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed for several seconds.
Epoch's stasis is the alternative against Black Hole and Purge, giving up the lifesteal and speed.
improvement: Nothing to swap: the winning core finished, nine kills and two deaths. Sound keep.

matchup: Duo was Riktor and TwinBlast against Mourn and Kira; Kira took first blood on Riktor, and Riktor killed Kira twice.
Mourn's Abduct pulls and Beguile mesmerizes, and Contagion heals and armors Mourn's allies.
Shock Therapy destroys shields and silences, and Skewer suppresses, lockdown TwinBlast can follow up on.
build: Stonewall and Warden's Faith stack physical armor against Kira and Crunch, and Warden's Faith cuts critical strike damage taken.
Transference pairs with Electrocute's shield: more movement speed and armor while shielded, and leftover shield returns as health.
The winning core is Dynamo, Xenia and Frosted Lure; Riktor built none of the three.
eternal: Nihil grows power and armor while Riktor keeps damaging heroes; From the Abyss regenerates health in hero combat.
Adaptive Plating adds armor matching the damage type taken.
The engine does not model Nihil; the field mostly runs Krix with Regenerative Tissue and Cannibalism on Riktor support.
augment: Zap O' 9-Chains makes the next basic attack after a cast zap nearby enemies, more damage in grouped fights.
Wanton Warden is the alternative: regenerate a share of damage taken, giving up the zap damage.
crest: Sanctification shields Riktor and nearby heroes, granting tenacity while the shield holds.
Visionary raises the ward cap, a fit for the most wards placed in the game.
improvement: Xenia for Stonewall shields an ally beside Riktor and adds magical armor, giving up health, physical armor and regeneration.
With one death and the most assists in the game, the current build is a sound keep.

matchup: Akeron was the lane opponent: zero kills, three deaths, and the second-most hero damage in the game.
Akeron heals off Crushing Maw and Consume bites, and Consume executes low-health targets.
Web Lash roots on hit, and the leap off a lashed wall knocks up and stuns.
build: Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone basic-attacking Greystone, such as Kira or Crunch.
Cybernetic Drive is the main flat magical armor in the build, beside Saphir's Mantle, against Akeron, Gideon and Mourn.
Overlord's cleave and Fire Blossom's burn add area damage while Greystone soaks damage.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health that grows with level; Regenerative Tissue regenerates after a stretch without hero damage.
Cannibalism paid once: one takedown all game, one stack of permanent health.
Feeding Frenzy is the second-minor alternative: attack speed per nearby enemy hero, with no takedowns needed.
augment: Tainted Oath blights enemies hit by Sacred Oath, cutting Akeron's healing and Mourn's Contagion healing.
Close Cut is the alternative: Make Way hits the nearest enemy harder, giving up the blight.
crest: Saphir's Mantle's Atlas grows size and health, damages nearby heroes and turns that damage into permanent max health.
Judgement is the alternative: an area hit that heals per hero struck, giving up the health growth.
improvement: The winning core is Overlord, Rapture and Aegis Of Agawar; Greystone finished Overlord and Aegis Of Agawar, not Rapture.
Rapture for Fire Blossom adds attack speed, omnivamp and close-range on-hit damage, giving up physical armor and the burn.

bde2abc7-2bb1-4fa0-984b-00adcb4782f7.headline: Sparrow and a deathless Lt. Belica ran the fights; the team took every Fangtooth and nine structures to one.

flags.text: Sparrow: 21 kills, 4 deaths, the most hero damage in the game, and the mid inhibitor.
Lt. Belica never died, killed Gadget six times and is credited with the mid outer and Core.
The team took three Fangtooths, Mini Prime, Genesis Core and Primal Fangtooth, and the enemy took none.
Four allies died within a minute of Mini Prime, and the next fight opened four against five.

focus.title: Five alive before a Prime
focus.action: Keep playing fights through Sparrow and Lt. Belica, and start a Prime only with all five alive, so the fight that follows opens five against five, not four.

9.call: Lt. Belica killed Gadget in mid while Sparrow killed Steel, Skylar and Boris on the duo side, two separate plays with no allied deaths. The team took the first Fangtooth within the minute.

19.5.call: The fight opened four against five with Riktor dead. Boris killed Feng Mao and Skylar killed Bayle, while Sparrow killed Steel, Boris, Skylar and Gadget. The team took the third Fangtooth within the next minute.

21.5.call: Sparrow killed Skylar, Steel and Boris on the duo side while Lt. Belica killed Akeron in mid, with no allied deaths. The team took the Genesis Core, and Sparrow is credited with the enemy duo inner tower within the minute.

27.9.call: Sparrow killed Skylar, Boris, Akeron and Gadget, and Feng Mao killed Steel, with no allied deaths. Bayle is credited with the offlane inner tower, Sparrow with the mid inhibitor and Lt. Belica with the Core within the next minute.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Fucking ruthless: 21 kills and the most hero damage in the game, 1588 per minute against a norm of 922.
Credited with the duo inner, mid inner and mid inhibitor. All 4 deaths came from Skylar, so Skylar was the one threat to track in every fight.
274e2cd8-94a0-427e-8c8d-a55037022e77: Did the frontline job: the most damage mitigated in the game at 40902, and 10 wards placed against a norm of 7.
Died to Boris in the enemy jungle outside any detected fight shortly before Mini Prime, and the next fight opened four against five.
Cleared 0 enemy wards while Steel placed 13. When the duo wave is shoved, sweep the duo-side river, with a sentry if one is equipped.
62236d47-dc4c-484d-9248-6a8da4bfea2c: Credited with two structures, the enemy duo outer and offlane inner towers, on 3 deaths, under the norm.
10 takedowns in the team's 40 kills, the lowest share on the team. Once the offlane opens, keep joining mid fights, as the Gadget kill before Primal Fangtooth did.
28eac1f2-8f16-4a46-b908-8e579747238a: Zero deaths, the only player in the game without one, and 6 kills on Gadget, who died 10 times, the most in the game. Shit-hot mid.
Hero damage ran 1145 per minute against a norm of 814; credited with the mid outer tower and the Core.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Most objective damage in the game at 35721 and the most assists at 12, and the team took every Fangtooth.
Killed Boris, Akeron and Gadget in the mid fight that went 3-1, with 3 deaths, under the norm.
4 wards placed, under the norm. If wards were equipped, spend the wards on the pit approaches before each Fangtooth and Prime.

matchup: Duo was Sparrow and Riktor against Skylar and Steel; Sparrow killed Skylar five times and Steel seven times.
Skylar killed Sparrow all four times and finished with nine kills, the most on the enemy team.
Steel's Shield Bash and Shield Slam both stun and Bull Rush knocks heroes back, so Steel's lockdown is the duo lane danger.
build: Every item except the Liberator crest carries critical chance, and Imperator makes critical strikes hit harder.
No item or the crest carries armor or health; Terminus and Liberator's shields are the only defense.
Tainted Rounds cuts healing on each target Sparrow basic-attacks, covering Akeron and Boris, the two top healers in the game.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Sparrow damages a hero below 30% health, with extra missiles from bonus attack speed.
Wind-Rider adds attack speed on leaving Stealth, which Heightened Senses supplies; Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill.
augment: Endless Hunt resets basic ability cooldowns on takedowns and adds permanent physical penetration; 21 kills and 2 assists fed the stacks.
Sun Shards is the field's higher-winning alternative: ricocheting basic attacks, giving up the resets and penetration.
crest: Liberator cleanses all debuffs and shields, an answer to Gadget's Security Gate root and Akeron's Web Lash root.
Pacifier is the field's higher-winning alternative: a dash and an empowered hit, giving up the cleanse.
improvement: Sound keep: 4 deaths, at the norm, with the most hero damage in the game.
The winning core is Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra; none was built, and this game gives no reason to switch.

matchup: Duo was Riktor and Sparrow against Steel and Skylar; Skylar took first blood on Riktor and killed Riktor three times.
Riktor killed Skylar twice, and Steel never killed Riktor.
Shock Therapy destroys shields: Steel's Cybernetic Shell and the shield Skylar's Equinox grants below 40% health.
build: Dynamo and Xenia are two of the three winning-core items; Frosted Lure is the missing third.
Tainted Charm cuts healing on enemy heroes near Riktor, covering Akeron and Boris, the two top healers in the game.
Unbroken Will and Xenia carry the magical armor against Gadget's and Steel's magical damage.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health growing with level; Regenerative Tissue regenerates after a stretch without hero damage.
Cannibalism adds permanent health per takedown; 12 takedowns fed the bonus.
Knell posts a higher field win rate on Riktor support: armor shred on hits, giving up the health stacking.
augment: Wanton Warden regenerates a share of damage taken, and Riktor took the third-most damage in the game.
Warden's Leash posts the highest field win rate of the three: Riplash also hooks allies, giving up the regeneration.
crest: Sanctification shields Riktor and nearby heroes, adds tenacity while the shield holds, and raises the ward cap.
Rift Walkers is the alternative: a dash that pulls nearby heroes, giving up the group shield.
improvement: If Skylar keeps finding Riktor, Frosted Lure for Unbroken Will adds physical armor and a slow, giving up magical armor and tenacity.

matchup: Akeron was the lane opponent: one kill each way, and Akeron finished 1/6/3 with the most healing in the game.
Akeron heals off Crushing Maw and Consume bites, and Consume bites execute low-health targets.
build: Citadel is the only physical armor in the build, and also cuts the physical armor of nearby enemy heroes.
Manta Scythe adds damage against isolated targets; Sky Splitter's current-health hits hurt most against high-health targets.
Vyzar Carapace's Shell Smash triggers on three stacks of Scorn, adding damage and a shield.
eternal: Thraex marks the last hero Bayle basic-attacked: more damage to that hero, less damage back.
Alpha's Court adds damage with no ally nearby; Ferocity stacks attack speed through hero combat.
Knell posts a higher field win rate on Bayle offlane: armor shred on hits, giving up the mark.
augment: Betrayer's Reqiuem makes Kingslayer uppercut every enemy around the target and lowers Kingslayer's cooldown.
Betrayer's Reqiuem holds the highest field win rate of the three Bayle offlane augments. Sound keep.
crest: Judgement is an area hit that heals per hero struck, with the first hero hit healing most.
Gravitum is the alternative: a long-range shot that grounds the first hero hit, giving up the heal.
improvement: Tainted Blade, from the winning core, for Vyzar Carapace adds anti-heal against Akeron's game-high healing, giving up Shell Smash.
The rest is a sound keep: 3 deaths, under the norm, and two structures credited.

matchup: Gadget was the mid opponent: Lt. Belica killed Gadget six times, and Gadget never killed Lt. Belica.
Gadget built Azure Core and Combustion, both max mana, so Neural Disruptor's missing-mana damage has a target.
build: Combustion and Wraith Leggings are two of the three winning-core items; Noxia is the missing third.
Caustica ignores a share of magical armor, which cuts through Steel's Crystalline Cuirass.
Oblivion Crown raises magical power by a quarter; Wraith Leggings adds ability damage on heroes below 40% health.
eternal: Vesh adds damage over time from ability damage on heroes.
The Tenth Seal and Millennia both raise ultimate damage, feeding Neural Disruptor.
Lotus posts a higher field win rate on Lt. Belica mid: random stacking bonuses over time and per takedown.
augment: Devastating Bombs adds Void Bomb damage against isolated targets.
Combat Veteran posts the higher field win rate: movement speed and passive experience, giving up the bomb damage.
crest: Epoch's stasis buys time against burst; zero deaths makes Epoch a sound keep.
Typhoon is the higher-winning field alternative: basic attacks stack attack speed, giving up the stasis.
improvement: Nothing to swap: zero deaths and the second-most hero damage in the game. Sound keep.
Noxia for Caustica adds max-health burst through a second ability hit, giving up magical armor penetration.

matchup: Boris was the jungle opponent: 3 kills and 8 deaths, with two of those kills on Riktor.
Boris's Ursine Burst grabs a hero and Primeval Roar fears nearby enemies.
The enemy ran three physical damage dealers, and no completed item carries armor.
build: Manta Scythe, Omen and The Perforator are the winning core, all three finished.
The Perforator ignores a share of physical armor and slows on ability damage.
Omen's empowered hit cuts non-ultimate cooldowns, bringing Reaping Dash back sooner.
eternal: Demiurge raises item stats and item-effect damage; Construct adds health and ability haste per level.
Bloatware adds damage and damage reduction per item; three completed items plus the Ortus crest kept the bonus small.
Demiurge holds the higher field win rate of the two most played Feng Mao jungle Eternals.
augment: Ichorous Glaive heals off unit kills, far more on Earth Shatter executions.
Imperial Duelist is the most played alternative: debuffed targets take more damage and deal less, giving up the healing.
crest: Ortus grants speed and physical power; takedowns inside the window add permanent power and refresh the window.
Ortus holds a higher field win rate than Nex, the most played Feng Mao jungle crest.
improvement: The winning core finished with 3 deaths, under the norm. Sound keep.
If Skylar or Boris start ending fights early, compare an armor item for Omen, giving up cooldown cuts and penetration.

d5078c37-98f7-4d2d-a57a-338670c048f1.headline: An early four-kill lead went to shit in the team's own jungle, where Sparrow and The Fey died in the same fight three times.

flags.text: Drongo killed Sparrow three times and The Fey twice, finishing with the game's most hero damage.
The enemy's second Fangtooth fell with no ally dead; Genesis Core followed a minute later.
The enemy scored the last six kills, and seven allied structures fell in under two minutes, Core included.
The four-kill early lead finished as a 68.4k to 78.4k gold deficit, three structures taken to ten lost.

focus.title: Shore up the duo side, then contest Fangtooth
focus.action: Play the duo side as three with the jungler until Drongo stops winning fights there, and when Fangtooth is up with all five alive, contest the pit as a group rather than concede it.

15.8.call: Feng Mao and Gideon had died in mid within the minute before, and Argus took the mid outer tower. Drongo then killed Sparrow and The Fey in the team's jungle, lost 0-2. After two mid deaths, giving ground on the duo side was the cheaper call.

17.4.call: Drongo killed Sparrow and Bayle killed The Fey in the team's jungle, lost 0-2, and Bayle killed Feng Mao outside any fight just before the enemy's first Fangtooth. Mini Prime went to the team a minute later, the right trade to look for.

23.8.call: Argus killed The Fey first; Sparrow, Scarlett and Feng Mao answered with kills on Argus, Drongo and Narbash before Bayle killed Feng Mao, won 3-2. Gideon took the enemy mid outer tower in the same window.

26.2.call: Right after the enemy's Fangtooth, Drongo killed The Fey and Argus killed Sparrow in the team's jungle, lost 0-2. With the pit already gone, the duo's job was grouping for Genesis Core, not trading.

29.2.call: Feng Mao killed Drongo, then Bayle killed The Fey, Feng Mao and Gideon across the mid and duo lanes, lost 1-3, Sparrow having died 46 seconds before. With a body down, two separate plays on two lanes were ones to give up, holding the inner towers together instead.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Seven kills, the team high, plus 7491 objective damage, the most on the team, and credit for the enemy duo outer tower.
Seven deaths against a norm under six, four to Bayle, who took the game-high nine kills; one came outside any fight just before the enemy's first Fangtooth.
Nine wards against a norm of 5.4. When Bayle leads the kill trade, start Fangtooth only with Gideon alongside, and ward the pit first.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: One death against a norm over three, 12.6 CS per minute against a norm of 9.5, and the most gold on the team.
First blood on Steel, and a rotation kill on Drongo on the duo lane right after The Fey died there.
Zero objective damage on the team's most gold. Once the enemy offlane outer is down, push the wave into the inner tower whenever Steel shows on another lane.
5ad0989b-03a9-463e-9a0a-4760477c2ac1: Hell of a damage game: 1148 hero damage per minute against a norm of 718, the most on the team.
Argus killed this mid three times, never died to this mid, earned the game's most gold and destroyed the team's mid outer tower and inhibitor.
Two rotation deaths, on the offlane and the duo lane, brought no prize within ninety seconds. Rotate off a pushed mid wave into a fight already called.
179dd4f4-6f37-4156-a454-1a7b790d74ad: Five deaths against a norm under four, three to Drongo, with hero damage at 538 per minute against a norm of 684.
Drongo built the same Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Tainted Rounds and out-earned this carry 15157 gold to 13495.
Two deaths came outside any fight, to Argus and Drongo. With both missing from the map, leave the duo wave until The Fey arrives.
41c33cbd-ae70-41d5-a32a-006838dcb153: Seven deaths against a norm under three, tied for the most in the game, and the first to fall in two fights.
Nine wards to Narbash's 14, none cleared, 1099 healing, and a hand in a quarter of the team's kills.
Four of the seven deaths went to Bayle, two on the mid lane. When Bayle is missing from the map, ward the river before joining a mid fight.

matchup: Bayle was the jungle opponent; the head-to-head kills ran three for Feng Mao and four for Bayle.
Dire Howl heals Bayle for a share of damage taken, and Salvation shields Bayle below 30% health.
Berserk fires when Bayle drops low, so Earth Shatter's execute is the clean finish.
build: Tainted Trident cuts healing by 45% on physical damage, against Bayle's Dire Howl heal and Narbash's healing.
Solstice carries both armors and is the only physical armor on the team against Drongo's physical damage.
The Perforator is the missing winning-core item: it ignores 30% of physical armor, against Steel's and Bayle's armor items.
eternal: Demiurge raises item stats and item-effect damage by 10%; Construct adds health and ability haste per level.
Bloatware adds damage and damage reduction per item, and four completed items fed the bonus.
Demiurge leans ahead of Lotus in the field for Feng Mao jungle, and Construct with Bloatware is Demiurge's best pair.
augment: Ichorous Glaive restores 4% missing health per unit kill, 35% on Earth Shatter executions.
Imperial Duelist is the field toss-up partner: against debuffed targets, deal 5% more damage and take 5% less, giving up healing.
crest: Ortus grants movement speed and physical power for 7s; takedowns inside that window add permanent physical power.
Ortus is the field's best Feng Mao jungle crest, clearly ahead of Nex, the most played.
improvement: The Perforator next completes the winning core, adding penetration and ability slows without selling Solstice's armor.
Sound keep on Demiurge, Ortus and Ichorous Glaive; the field gives no edge to a swap.

matchup: Steel was the lane opponent: first blood went to Scarlett, and Steel finished with the most damage mitigated in the game.
Steel's Shield Bash stuns, Bull Rush knocks heroes back, and Shield Slam knocks up and stuns.
Tainted Guard cuts the healing of any hero basic-attacking Steel and applies a bleed.
build: Mutilator's Devour applies max-health damage on ability hits, suited to Steel's health-stacked build.
Terminus turns lifesteal overhealing into a shield, which Tainted Guard's healing cut blunts against Steel.
No completed item or the crest carries magical armor, against an enemy team with three magical damage dealers.
eternal: Knell shreds both armors with Rust stacks on hits against heroes and returns 75% of the armor shredded.
Peal applies maximum Rust after Swan Song; Patina with Fracture is the field's best pair.
Knell is the field's best Scarlett offlane Eternal, clearly ahead of Marrow.
augment: Volcaic Slam makes Empowered Cindara leave an eruption that damages and slows by 40%.
Volcaic Slam is clearly the field's best Scarlett offlane augment. Sound keep.
crest: Liberator's active cleanses all debuffs and grants a shield, an answer to Steel's stuns and Drongo's Gag Grenade silence.
Gravitum leans ahead in the field: a long-range shot that grounds the first hero hit, giving up the cleanse.
improvement: The winning core is Alternator, Earthshaker and The Perforator; none was built.
One death and the team's most gold: no defensive swap was forced. If magical damage starts landing, magical armor replaces Rebirth's revive.

matchup: Argus was the mid opponent, a Vesh mage on Tithe of Death and Mind Rot, finishing 7/2/5.
Dread Nova stuns, Ether Crystal slows, and Synaptic Obliterator beams hit harder on targets missing health.
build: Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings are the full winning core, all three finished.
Spellbreaker's Veil blocks the next ability on a cooldown and adds magical armor against Argus's damage.
Wraith Leggings adds 12% ability damage against heroes below 40% health.
eternal: Vesh adds damage over time from ability damage on heroes; Tithe of Death restores mana and stacks ability haste on takedowns.
Phylactery speeds cooldowns and shields after Black Hole; The Tenth Seal with Millennia is the field's best Vesh pair.
Vesh holds the best odds in a field toss-up with Demiurge and Xyris on Gideon mid.
augment: Event Horizon adds max-health damage to enemies in Cosmic Rift's center.
Abyssal Mantle leans ahead in the field: a shield on activating Black Hole, giving up the Cosmic Rift damage.
crest: Soulbearer's Anima grants a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed.
Soulbearer is the field's best Gideon mid crest, clearly ahead of Epoch. Sound keep.
improvement: Full winning core and the team's most hero damage: sound keep on the build.

matchup: Duo was Sparrow and The Fey against Drongo and Narbash; Drongo killed Sparrow three times, Sparrow killed Drongo twice.
Drongo's Wastelander bleed deals max-health damage on crits and ability hits, and Shrapnel Cannon shreds physical armor.
Narbash's Thunk stuns, and Narbash had the most healing in the game.
build: Tainted Rounds cuts healing on basic-attacked targets, against Narbash's healing.
No item or the Pacifier crest carries armor or health against Drongo's physical damage.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Sparrow damages a hero below 30% health.
Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill; Wind-Rider adds attack speed after leaving Heightened Senses' Stealth.
Thraex and Weald are a field toss-up on Sparrow carry; Forage with Wind-Rider is Weald's best pair.
augment: Endless Hunt resets basic ability cooldowns on takedowns and adds permanent physical penetration; five takedowns fed the stacks.
Sun Shards leans ahead in the field: ricocheting basic attacks, giving up the resets and penetration.
crest: Pacifier dashes and empowers the next physical hit, stronger on targets below 20% health.
Pacifier leans ahead of Eviscerator, the most played Sparrow carry crest. Sound keep.
improvement: The winning core is Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra; Sky Splitter was the one finished.
Spectra next adds attack speed and Prisma hits that grow with the target's missing health.

matchup: Duo was The Fey and Sparrow against Narbash and Drongo; before minute ten, the enemy duo died once, the allied duo never.
Bayle killed The Fey four times; Skull Crusher leaps in, and Cursed Edge's third slash knocks up and stuns.
Narbash's Thunk knocks back and stuns, and Narbash died once all game with twelve assists.
build: Combustion, Tainted Scepter and Megacosm are damage items; the support winning core is Crescelia, Timewarp and Astral Catalyst.
Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage, against Narbash, the game's top healer.
Megacosm and Tainted Scepter add health, but no item carries armor against Bayle's and Drongo's physical damage.
eternal: Aion turns spell damage on heroes into gold; Philosopher drips gold and Perfection adds ability haste above 85% health.
The engine does not model support Eternals; the field's The Fey support toss-up is Aion, Lotus and Vesh.
augment: Wild Growth gives Bramble Patch 30% more range, the field's most played pick.
Natural Infusion leans ahead in the field: Harvest Nettles hits on heroes stack ability haste, giving up the range.
crest: Epoch's Stasis Device puts The Fey in stasis, a few-games pick on The Fey support.
Tranquility and Silentium are the field's toss-up: gold over time and a third ward, which Epoch lacks.
improvement: With the lowest gold on the team, a support crest's gold income is the swap to test, giving up the stasis.
If Bayle keeps killing The Fey, an armor item next covers the physical damage the build leaves open.
